The paper's central RQ2 finding — 'the only contemporaneous verbatim scope statement... records out-of-scope recognition' (OpenAI–Hugging Face D2) — is stated in the main text as a clean per-unit fact, but the underlying coded-evidence row notes the quotes are drawn across multiple runs and are 'reported for some of the ~700 participating agents, not per run,' a representativeness caveat that is not surfaced where the finding is asserted in §IV.C and §V.
strengths: Extensive cross-checking shows the manuscript's reported counts (40/5 baseline, R08/R02/R10 support tallies, D2 evidence-type breakdown, D4 stopping-mechanism groupings, D5 branch counts) are traceable to and consistent with the released coded_evidence.csv and supporting result files.

The codebook gives explicit, falsifiable decision rules (documented/contradicted/unknown; D5 branch definitions; D2 evidence-type and strict-vs-baseline rules) rather than vague qualitative judgment calls.

Limitations and Appendix sections are candid about single-coder coding, AI-assisted revisions, unreachable sources, and the non-representativeness of the unit set, and the sensitivity/rule-variant analysis (S0–S6, flip analysis) is a genuine transparency effort.

Section III.D reports no completed independent human coding of the current matrix or D5 branches. Seven net status changes and all branch annotations originate with AI agents; the 44/45 same-document AI consistency result does not establish coding reliability.

The central two-organization finding depends on proposition granularity that the codebook does not operationalize. Hugging Face D4 combines organization-specific responses and requires each source to support that entire conjunction, while Opus 4.7 D4 treats backend cessation as a qualification and counts support for retrospective detection alone.

Section IV.C concludes that the disclosures cannot answer RQ2 for most units, but its analysis codes scope statements without a parallel coding instrument or complete trace for reality recognition, the other component of RQ2.

Data and Code Availability asserts an archived, reproducible release, but supplies no archive identifier, confirmed command or pinned environment. The provided excerpts cannot reproduce the full organization, selection and sensitivity analyses.

The supplied submission is uncompiled Markdown with unresolved citation keys rather than the required IEEE two-column manuscript with numeric citations. Compliance with the six-page main-text limit and rendered table readability is unverified.

Sections II and Appendix D establish extensive overlap with prior incident comparisons, reporting dimensions and evidence methods. The remaining novelty is a bounded corpus-specific audit artifact whose current release and recount inconsistencies weaken the principal incremental contribution.
strengths: The topic is directly relevant to an AI-security workshop, especially the distinction between reachability, scope interpretation and actual authorization.
Appendix B and the supplied coded data expose all 45 statuses, source locators and substantive qualifications rather than presenting only aggregate findings.
The manuscript consistently distinguishes documentary support from incident truth and avoids prevalence estimates, causal defense claims and treating dependent units as independent samples.
The D2 evidence profiles separate contemporaneous statements, reported reasoning and elicited answers, preserving evidence that challenges the reported interpretations.
The C/N/P branches distinguish credential use, data access and persistent changes, including explicit qualifications for Hugging Face datasets and refused AISI contributions.
The manuscript candidly reports AI involvement, coding revisions, source-access limitations and sensitivity to alternative status rules.
